content:
Last Friday (the 21st), during the sentencing of the Hong Kong Alliance case, police took a woman who was queuing to observe the hearing away in a police vehicle in the early hours of the morning. In response to inquiries, the police said the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent."

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of wearing a shirt with somewhat seditious intent," and took her away in a police vehicle. While the officers took the woman away, several officers kept directing journalists to leave, saying "take you to the press area," and pulled the orange cordon towards the direction of Ying Wa Street. Once the woman had boarded the police vehicle, they put away the cordon. A "court-watching volunteer" who had been queuing near the woman said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

集誌社 (The Collective) inquired with the police about the reason for the woman's removal and whether an arrest had been made. The police replied this morning (the 24th) that during a security operation in the area of the West Kowloon Courts on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent," and was detained for investigation.
